result.topic_en: Computation of the potential of two parallel charged discs of radius R at distance 2ε: the first part V_1 is expanded for x > R, and the second part V_2 is obtained by integrating over each disc, giving 2πP_1(φ+φ').
result.transcription:
Für $x > R$ ergiebt sich
$V_1 = 2\pi [-\varepsilon-] R \{ 2\varepsilon - \frac{2\varepsilon R^2}{x^2} + \frac{2\varepsilon^2 R^2}{x^4} + \dots$
$= 4\pi R \varepsilon \{ 1 - \frac{R^2}{x^2} + \frac{\varepsilon R^2}{x^4} + \dots$
Der zweite Theil der Potentialfunktion
$V_2$ wird gefunden durch Integration
des Ausdruckes
$P_1 R \iint \frac{r\,dr\,d\vartheta}{\sqrt{(R^2-r^2)(r^2+x^2)}} + P_1 R \iint \frac{r\,dr\,d\vartheta}{\sqrt{(R^2-r^2)(r^2+(x+2\varepsilon)^2)}}$
Von dieser Summe braucht man vor
der Hand wieder nur den ersten [-Theil-] {+Summanden+}
zu entwickeln da der zweite ihm
vollkommen analog gebildet ist.
$\int_0^{2\pi} \frac{r\,dr\,d\vartheta}{\sqrt{(R^2-r^2)(r^2+x^2)}} = 2\pi \int \frac{r\,dr}{\sqrt{(R^2-r^2)(r^2+x^2)}}$
$\int \frac{r\,dr}{\sqrt{(R^2-r^2)(r^2+x^2)}} = \arctan \sqrt{\frac{x^2+r^2}{R^2-r^2}} + C$
mithin
$\int_0^R \frac{r\,dr}{\sqrt{(R^2-r^2)(r^2+x^2)}} = \frac{\pi}{2} - \arctan \frac{x}{R}$
$= \arctan \frac{R}{x} = \varphi$
mithin
$V_2 = 2\pi [-\varphi-] P_1^R \left(\arctan \frac{R}{x} + \arctan \frac{R}{x+2\varepsilon}\right)$
$= 2\pi P_1 (\varphi + \varphi')$
Das Gesammtpotential wird [-mithin-]
also gegeben durch
$V = 2\pi P_R (x(\sec\varphi - \sec\varphi') - 2\varepsilon \sec\varphi + 2\varepsilon)$
$+ 2\pi P_1^R (\varphi + \varphi')$

methods.what: Series expansion of the first potential part V_1 for x > R in powers of R/x
Second potential part as a sum of double integrals over the two discs
Antiderivative of r/sqrt((R^2-r^2)(r^2+x^2)) as an arctan
Definite integral from 0 to R evaluates to arctan(R/x)
Second potential part in terms of the angles φ and φ'
